problem_statement: A fixed-size Array offers no way to insert an element at an arbitrary index. The required interface is Array::InsertAt(index), which makes room and returns a pointer to the inserted slot for the caller to fill in (returning nullptr when the array is full or when index is greater than the current length), and Array::InsertAt(index, entry), which inserts a copy of an entry at the given index, shifting existing elements at and after that index rightward, returning kErrorNone on success, kErrorInvalidArgs when index is greater than the length, and kErrorNoBufs when the array is already full. Inserting an entry that is itself a reference into the array must remain correct even when that referenced element is shifted during the insert.
